prompt: A plain documentary colour photograph of a crewed lunar lander standing landed on a grey airless plain: a 30-metre-tall steel ship, seen whole from its footpads to its nose, from about 80 metres away, standing left of centre. The ship is a tall stainless-steel cylinder about 7 metres across, rounded at the top into a blunt dome nose. One side of the hull, the windward side, is covered in a field of black hexagonal heat-shield tiles, a few chipped and pale at the edges, and the rest is bare dull steel with horizontal weld seams and soft oil-canning dents. Dark soot stains the base around the engines and fades up the hull in streaks. Four long angled steel landing legs, each ending in a round footpad; all four touch the ground and are pressed into the dust with a small rim of pushed-up regolith. Engine bells under the ship are cold and dark, nothing glows. Light: one hard sun about 30 degrees above the horizon, exactly to the right, at 90 degrees to the line of sight. The key effect: the cylinder is split vertically down its whole length by a sharp line, its right half brightly sunlit dull steel, its left half in shadow, and that shadow half is not black but very dimly lit by warm grey light reflected up off the sunlit ground, so the weld seams and dents on the dark side are just barely readable, lighter toward the bottom of the hull and darker toward the top where it sees less ground. The ship's sharp black shadow lies along the ground to the left, and every leg, rock and footprint casts a parallel black shadow to the left. Ground: bare grey regolith, fine dust and scattered small rocks, a radial scoured fan of smoother lighter dust swept out from beneath the engines, footprints and two thin wheel tracks running in from the right. Parked inside the ship's cast shadow on the ground to the left of the ship is a small two-wheeled metal handcart with a few tool boxes on it, seen only dimly by the ground's reflected light, a witness of scale. Sky: flat featureless black above the sharp horizon, no stars, no Earth, no moon, no planet, no gradient, no haze. Lettering: one small black stencilled marking on the bare steel near the base, reading exactly "NO STEP", nothing else written. Camera: standing eye height about 1.6 metres, level, verticals vertical, 40mm lens, deep focus to the horizon. The whole ship fits in the portrait frame with ground below the footpads and black sky above the nose. True colour, matte, unretouched, shadows left dark and not opened up, no added grain, no film border.
